svg.title: The Free plan's two clocks, the calendar and the credits, beside the Paid plan and Always Free offers
svg.desc: Timeline from 0 to 12 months after sign-up, as of 2026-10-24. Free plan: a bar from 0 to 6 months; it ends at 6 months or sooner if the credits run out, and then the account closes. Credits, $100 plus up to $100 more: a solid bar from 0 to 6 months, up to $200 over 6 months on the Free plan, as AWS's Free Tier page says; then a dashed, unfilled bar from 6 to 12 months for leftover credits after an upgrade, whose expiry AWS pages give as 6 or 12 months after sign-up. Paid plan: a bar across all 12 months and beyond; it never closes for lack of credits, and usage beyond credits is billed. Always Free: monthly allowances on both plans with no end date. After the Free plan closes the account, AWS keeps content for 90 days; upgrading in that time restores access and leftover credits apply to later bills.
svg.text: The Free Tier now: two plans, and the Free plan's two clocks
A new account, months after sign-up. Terms as of 2026-10-24; check the AWS Free Tier page.

path.title: Always Free: Monthly allowances on both plans, with no end date

svg.text: Monthly allowances on both plans, with no end date
After the Free plan closes the account, AWS keeps your content for 90 days; upgrading within that time restores access,
and leftover credits apply to later bills. When they expire, AWS pages disagree: two FAQ answers say 6 months, two FAQ
answers and the Free Tier terms say 12; our own account's Credits page showed 12. Check your own Credits page.
Sources: AWS Free Tier page, FAQ and terms; Billing User Guide, "Choosing a plan"; our own Free plan account, 2026-10-23.
